findings.description: jwt.decode only base64-decodes the token and never checks the signature. SECRET is loaded but never used to verify. Also, decode returns null for malformed tokens, so claims.sub throws a TypeError that is forwarded as a 500 instead of a 401.
findings.scenario: Attacker builds an unsigned or arbitrarily signed token with payload {"sub":"<admin id>"} and sends 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. It is accepted and req.user becomes that user. A token like 'Bearer abc' gives claims=null and a 500.
findings.fix: const claims = jwt.verify(token, SECRET, { algorithms: ['HS256'] }); and in the catch for verification errors respond 401 instead of next(err).

findings.description: `req.user.role = 'admin'` assigns rather than compares. The condition is always truthy, so every authenticated user passes requireAdmin and is also mutated to role admin in memory (persisted if req.user is later saved).
findings.scenario: A normal user with role 'user' calls an admin-guarded route and gets through; the 403 branch is unreachable.

findings.description: The target user id comes from req.params.id and is not checked against req.user (the acting identity) or an admin role. revokeSessions itself performs no authorization, and the module does not enforce requireAdmin on it.
findings.scenario: Any authenticated user calls the revoke route with another user's id and logs that user out; combined with the bypasses above, anyone can do it.
findings.fix: Require req.user.id === req.params.id or req.user.role === 'admin' before listing and deleting, and wire requireAdmin or an ownership check on the route.

findings.description: forEach with an async callback does not wait for the deletes. The response is sent before they finish, and a failing db.sessions.delete becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which can crash Node 15+ and is never reported to the client. `revoked: total` reports the number listed, not the number actually deleted.
findings.scenario: If delete throws for the 3rd session, the client still receives {revoked: N} with success, and the process may terminate with an unhandledRejection. The session may remain valid.
findings.fix: await Promise.all(sessions.map(s => db.sessions.delete(s.id))); wrap the handler in try/catch or an async error wrapper, and respond only after completion.

findings.description: Revocation is capped at `limit` (default 50) sessions, so a revoke-all endpoint leaves the remaining sessions active when a user has more than that.
findings.scenario: User has 120 sessions and the call with no limit revokes only 50; the rest stay valid.
findings.fix: Delete all sessions for the user (e.g. a deleteByUser call) or loop until none remain; do not apply the pagination limit to revocation.

findings.description: SECRET is exported from the auth module, widening the exposure of the signing key for no stated need.
findings.scenario: Any module that requires this file can read the signing secret and might log or leak it.
